config.documentTitleFull: WRITTEN REQUEST TO THE OFFICE OF THE DISTRICT ATTORNEY GENERAL TO PREPARE A PETITION FOR EXPUNCTION OF A CONVICTION FOR ILLEGAL REGISTRATION OR VOTING, UNDER T.C.A. § 40-32-107(c) WITH PROCEDURE AT T.C.A. § 40-32-108

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Expunction of a conviction for illegal registration or voting where fifteen years have elapsed since completion of the sentence.

The conditions: fifteen years elapsed, every sentence requirement fulfilled, the offence occurred prior to any conviction for an expunction-ineligible offence, and no previous grant of expunction under subsection (a), (b) or (c).
The single named offence this subsection reaches. It reaches no other elections or fraud provision.
The petition goes to the convicting court and the appropriate court clerk's fee is charged.
The office of the district attorney general must prepare the petition and the proposed order and give them to the petitioner to file with the clerk.

The rebuttable presumption is keyed only to petitioners eligible under the enumerated paragraphs of subsection (a)(1), so no presumption applies here and the court weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety.
The certificate that must be attached before an order of expunction may be entered.
Expunction restores the person, in contemplation of law, to the status occupied before arrest, indictment, information, trial and conviction.

verificationStatute.description: Notarization is not prescribed by the procedure section and no verification statute exists to cite for a written request. The citation is left null and the silence is recorded in sourceSilences.

counselFlags: The generated artifact is the participant's own written request to the office of the district attorney general, together with the participant's controlled eligibility record. It is not the statutory petition and it is not the proposed order: T.C.A. § 40-32-108(e) requires both of those to be prepared by that office and given to the petitioner to be filed with the clerk. LegalEase does not draft, complete, sign or hold out either instrument as its own, and does not make the district attorney general's legal determination.

This is not official_pdf_fill, because no participant form exists: neither Tennessee state form index publishes an expunction form of any kind, and the state bureau's order form is a court order carrying an approved-for-entry block with signature lines for defence, the district attorney general and the judge. It is not process_guidance either, because a genuine participant-facing written submission exists and its destination, addressee and operative content are all determined.

LegalEase does not obtain the district attorney general's agreement, does not negotiate with that office, does not prepare or sign its petition or proposed order, does not create the certificate or the order the state bureau requires, does not create a clerk certification, makes no judicial finding, certifies no eligibility and promises neither filing nor relief. Refusal, opposition or disputed eligibility routes to an attorney handoff, and the participant still receives the generated request, the controlled factual record and the instructions before that handoff.

The certificate under T.C.A. § 40-32-102(c) is required on this route and an order must not be entered unless it is attached. It is a court instrument completed by court staff; this packet does not generate it, does not complete it and does not assert it has been obtained.

The fifteen-year wait is the longest in the chapter — three times the misdemeanour and Class E felony period and half again the Class C and D felony period — and it attaches to a single named offence rather than to an offence class. The clock runs from completion of the sentence, which means every fine, restitution amount, court cost and other assessment paid and every term of imprisonment, probation and condition of release completed. Anything outstanding means the sentence is not complete and the clock has not started.
This subsection reaches one named offence and no other elections or fraud provision. An unresolved identification of the conviction's exact section is handed off to an attorney rather than guessed.

Expunction under this subsection is not restoration of voting rights. That is a separate remedy under separate machinery, how the two interact was not established from the adopted authority chain, and nothing is asserted about it — which matters, because restoration is the outcome most participants on this route are actually seeking.
Subsection (c) is not reached by the rebuttable presumption, so no presumption applies.

No fee figure is quoted anywhere in this packet. The clerk's fee applies but the source records no retrievable amount, and the filing-fee field is left null rather than filled with a circulating number.
No indigency or fee-waiver provision appears anywhere in the governing sections. None is asserted and the fee-waiver field is left null.
Notarization is not prescribed by the procedure section and no verification statute exists to cite, so verificationStatute.citation is left null and the request carries an ordinary signature block.

Whether a district attorney general's office will prepare a petition on request, how long it takes, and whether any office publishes its own request form are all unestablished. T.C.A. § 40-32-108(e) makes preparation that office's duty, but no statewide request form is published on any official site and the practice interval is not established. Recorded as a blocked component.

Court timing carried from the pin: the clerk serves the petition on the district attorney general, who may submit recommendations within 60 days with a copy to the petitioner and may file evidence under seal, and the court may not order sooner than 61 days after service. After a denial there is no further petition for at least two years. None of that is asserted in this letter, which precedes the petition.

Recorded open question from the pin: the prior-expunction bars across the subsections of T.C.A. § 40-32-107 are asymmetric on the enacted text and the asymmetry cannot be resolved from it. This packet reports the participant's own answer and states which bars the governing subsection actually contains. It asserts no conclusion about a subsection that is silent and does not tell a participant a route is closed on the strength of a bar the statute does not impose.

Self-help stop conditions: The office of the district attorney general declines to prepare the petition, or indicates it will oppose. Self-help stops and the participant is handed off to an attorney; the participant keeps the generated request, the controlled factual record and the instructions. Eligibility is disputed by the district attorney general's office. That is a contested determination for that office and, on filing, for the court; it is handed off to an attorney rather than argued in the packet. Any other conviction anywhere on the record, including federal and out-of-state convictions that would be ineligible in Tennessee. Handed off to an attorney before anything is sent. Any unpaid court costs, fines, restitution or other assessments, which mean the sentence is not complete. The participant is directed to the convicting court's clerk to resolve the balance before the route reopens. Any borderline offence whose exact section cannot be matched against the current eligible list. Handed off to an attorney. Federal, military, tribal or out-of-state records, immigration consequences and any security-clearance question, each of which is referred out because Tennessee expunction does not reach them. Any question whether the conviction was under T.C.A. § 2-19-107 rather than another elections or fraud provision. The route reaches only that section, so an unresolved identification is handed off to an attorney rather than guessed. Any collateral question about restoration of voting rights, which is a separate remedy under separate machinery and is referred out.

correspondence.subjectLine: Request under T.C.A. § 40-32-108(e) that your office prepare a petition for expunction of a conviction under T.C.A. § 2-19-107, pursuant to T.C.A. § 40-32-107(c)
correspondence.salutation: To the Office of the District Attorney General for {judicialDistrict}:
bodyParagraphs: My name is {senderName}. I am writing to ask your office to prepare a petition for expunction and a proposed order under T.C.A. § 40-32-108(e), so that I can then file them with the clerk of the convicting court under T.C.A. § 40-32-108(a). I am not asking your office to reach any conclusion for me. I am asking it to prepare the instruments the statute assigns to it, and I set out below the facts I rely on so that your office can make its own determination.

The conviction is in {convictingCourt}, in {judicialDistrict}. The case number as I read it from my own record is {docketNumber}. The offence and the exact statutory section as they appear on the judgment are: {offenceAndSection}. My state control number is [STATE CONTROL NUMBER — SENDER READS IT FROM THEIR OWN CRIMINAL HISTORY AND ENTERS IT HERE BEFORE SENDING].

I rely on T.C.A. § 40-32-107(c), which reaches a conviction for illegal registration or voting under T.C.A. § 2-19-107 and no other elections or fraud provision. My own answers on each condition are: on whether the conviction is under that section — {confirmedSection}; on the date I completed the sentence — {sentenceCompletionDate}; on whether fifteen years have elapsed since that date, measured as at the date of this letter — {fifteenYears}; on whether every fine, restitution amount, court cost and other assessment is paid and every term of imprisonment, probation and condition of release completed — {allComplete}; on whether the offence occurred prior to any conviction for an offence that is ineligible for expunction — {predatesIneligible}; and on whether I have previously been granted expunction under subsection (a), (b) or (c) — {priorExpunction}.

I record one thing I am not asking for. I understand that expunction under this subsection is not restoration of my voting rights, that restoration is a separate remedy under separate machinery, and that nothing in this request asserts how the two interact. I also understand that this subsection is not reached by the rebuttable presumption, so the court weighs my interest against the best interests of justice and public safety.

I understand that once your office prepares the petition and the proposed order, I file them with the clerk of the convicting court and pay the appropriate clerk's fee, and that the clerk then serves the petition on your office. I understand that this letter is not the petition, that it starts no statutory clock, and that nothing in it binds your office to my reading of my own record. Please send your written response to my mailing address shown at the top of this letter.
enclosures: [COPY OF THE JUDGMENT SHOWING THE OFFENCE AND ITS EXACT STATUTORY SECTION — SENDER ENCLOSES A COPY ONLY]
[COPY OF WHATEVER RECORD THE SENDER HOLDS SHOWING THE DATE THE SENTENCE WAS COMPLETED — SENDER ENCLOSES A COPY ONLY]

provenance.registryExcerpt: Expunction of the conviction record. Under T.C.A. § 40-32-110 the petitioner is entitled to have all public records of the expunged conviction destroyed in the manner set out in the chapter, restoring the person in contemplation of law to the status occupied before arrest, indictment, information, trial and conviction. A person convicted of illegal registration or voting under T.C.A. § 2-19-107, where fifteen years have elapsed since completion of the sentence, every sentence requirement has been fulfilled, the offence occurred prior to any conviction for an expunction-ineligible offence, and the person has not previously been granted expunction under § 40-32-107(a), (b) or (c). The fifteen-year wait is the longest in the chapter — three times the misdemeanour and Class E felony period and half again the Class C and D felony period — and it attaches to a single named offence rather than to an offence class. Codified through Public Chapter 608 and untouched by Public Chapters 719, 930 and 1061. Subsection (c) is not reached by the § 40-32-108(d)(2) rebuttable presumption, which is keyed only to petitioners eligible under § 40-32-107(a)(1)(A) to (E), so no presumption applies and the court weighs the interest of the petitioner against the best interests of justice and public safety. Venue: The convicting court, under § 40-32-108(a). The request goes to the district attorney general for that judicial district. A person with convictions in more than one judicial district deals with each separately. Destination: The office of the district attorney general for the judicial district of the convicting court, then the clerk of that court — Once the district attorney general's office prepares the petition and proposed order, the petitioner files them with the clerk of the convicting court under § 40-32-108(a) and pays the clerk's fee under T.C.A. § 8-21-401. Exclusion: Any conviction other than a violation of T.C.A. § 2-19-107. The subsection reaches that one named offence and no other elections or fraud provision. Exclusion: Any case where fewer than fifteen years have elapsed since completion of the sentence, measured at the time the petition is filed. Exclusion: Any case where a sentence requirement remains unfulfilled, including any unpaid fine, restitution amount, court cost or other assessment, any uncompleted term of imprisonment or probation, or any unmet condition of supervised or unsupervised release. Exclusion: Any case where the offence did not occur prior to a conviction for a criminal offence that is ineligible for expunction, including federal convictions and convictions in other states that would be ineligible in Tennessee. Exclusion: A person previously granted expunction under T.C.A. § 40-32-107(a), (b) or (c) for another criminal offence. Subsection (c)(1)(D) names exactly those three and does not name subsection (d). Exclusion: Restoration of voting rights. That is a separate remedy under separate machinery and is not what expunction under this subsection does. Waiting period — Every § 40-32-107(c) route: Fifteen years from completion of the sentence imposed for the offence being expunged, measured at the time of filing the petition. This is the longest waiting period in the chapter. Waiting period — When the clock starts: On completion of the sentence, which means every fine, restitution amount, court cost and other assessment paid, any term of imprisonment or probation completed, and all conditions of supervised or unsupervised release met. Anything outstanding means the sentence is not complete and the clock has not started. Waiting period — Court timing: The court may not order sooner than 61 days after the petition is served on the district attorney general, who has 60 days to submit recommendations. Waiting period — After a denial: No further petition for at least two years from the date of the denial, under § 40-32-108(d)(3).
